rules.statement: Don't write a record from an audit or event handler to the database inside the operation that raised it; add it to a bounded in-memory queue that a hosted service writes in batches.
rules.why: An inline write adds a database round trip to every audited operation, and a failed write would fail the operation.
rules.check: Look for event or audit handlers that call a store, DbContext or SaveChanges directly in the request path instead of enqueueing for a background writer.

rules.statement: When a bounded in-memory queue is full, drop the new item, count the drop, and log the count once per flush instead of blocking or logging each drop.
rules.why: The producing operation must never wait on the queue, and one log entry per flush shows how many items were lost without flooding the log.
rules.check: Look at bounded queues or channels fed from a request path: check that a full queue doesn't block the producer or throw, that drops are counted, and that the count is logged per flush, not per item.

rules.statement: A background batch writer writes each batch in its own unit of work, keeps a failed batch and writes it first on the next flush, and makes the insert idempotent under a unique key so that a save that committed but reported failure adds nothing twice.
rules.why: Retrying a batch without idempotency would duplicate records whose save had actually committed.
rules.check: Look at batch flush code: check that a failed batch is kept for retry rather than discarded, and that the store skips duplicates under a unique index on the record's identifier.

rules.statement: A hosted service that flushes held data when the host stops performs that final flush exactly once, with concurrent or repeated stop calls sharing the same flush.
rules.why: The host may stop a service twice, and each held record must be written once.
rules.check: Look at StopAsync implementations that flush: check that a second or concurrent call awaits the same flush task instead of starting another one.

rules.statement: A periodic prune service runs on a PeriodicTimer created from the registered TimeProvider, removes rows in bounded batches each in its own unit of work while a batch comes back full, and logs any failure other than host shutdown, then retries at the next tick, so that only the stopping token ends it.
rules.why: A timeout or transient failure must not end retention enforcement for the rest of the process lifetime, and bounded batches keep each transaction small.
rules.check: Look at prune or cleanup hosted services: check for unbounded deletes, use of Task.Delay or the system clock instead of TimeProvider, and catch blocks that let a non-cancellation exception end the loop.

rules.statement: In a batched prune, treat a batch whose save lost a concurrency race to another replica's prune as a full batch and continue, rather than as a failure.
rules.why: The other replica removed rows of that batch, so more rows may still be waiting to be pruned.
rules.check: Look at how a prune loop handles concurrency exceptions such as DbUpdateConcurrencyException: check that it continues the loop instead of stopping or logging an error.

rules.statement: When a value copied into an indexed column of limited length can be longer than the column, store null for an optional field and the leading characters for a required one, and keep the full value in the stored JSON document.
rules.why: The save must not fail on an over-long value, and the complete value stays available in the whole record.
rules.check: Look at mappings that copy fields from a document into length-limited indexed columns: check that over-long values are handled and not passed through unchecked.

rules.statement: Keyset-paginate time-ordered lists on the timestamp with a unique surrogate identifier as the tie-breaker, over an index that leads with the filter field, then the timestamp, then the identifier, and put both last-item values in the opaque cursor.
rules.why: Records with the same timestamp would otherwise be skipped or repeated across pages.
rules.check: Look at paged queries ordered by a time column: check for a unique tie-breaker in both the ORDER BY and the cursor, and for an index that matches.

rules.statement: When a tenant-addressed endpoint reads data that isn't covered by the tenant query filter, add the tenant as an explicit criterion of every query, and leave out rows that have no tenant.
rules.why: Without the tenant criterion, a lookup would return other tenants' records.
rules.check: Look at queries over data without a tenant filter, such as data that outlives its tenant, that are reached through a tenant route: check for an explicit TenantId predicate.
